layer_reason: The paired profiling shows the deficit is per-program latency (3.0 us per block vs 0.4 us useful vector work, 1024 blocks over 40 cores) rather than vector throughput or a changed memory layout; the cheapest controllable lever is how many bytes one program handles, which needs no new layout, no cache and no non-Triton compute.
simulator_incremental_judgment: Hotspots add location, not separation: the source_conditional region (lines 88-138, instruction_time 89 us) and the function-entry region (13.21 us wait instruction) rank where instructions sit but cannot separate launch/setup from tile work. The normalized per-core timeline adds the decisive lane-level distinction: MTE3 productive 49.9% / wait-only 34.3% / idle 15.8%, VECTOR productive only 10.1% / wait-only 30.3% / idle 59.6%, MTE2 productive 35.9% / idle 64.1%. This rejects a vector-throughput ceiling and shows each lane idle while another owns the window, i.e. short serial load->vector->store chains, supporting the per-program fixed-latency hypothesis; the paired profiling (Block Dim 1024 vs reference 40, per-block aiv_time 3.0 us vs 0.4 us useful vector) supplies the quantitative program-count lever. Incremental judgment: the simulator is the disambiguation between 'compute bound' (rejected) and 'per-program latency with little intra-program overlap' (supported), while the counting lever comes from profiling. Neither proves a dependency stall; the ratios are partial-window fractions with absolute_time_qualified=false, so the edit is accepted only if the differential program-count prediction holds.
